description: A patient whose insula was destroyed on both sides by herpes simplex encephalitis, interviewed as reported by Damasio, kept a sense of self and answered questions about his own mind and awareness coherently, against the view that the posterior insula is the basis of the subjective self.
limitations: A single case, reported second hand from a congress talk. It bears on the insular version of cortical theories only.

sources.quote: This case disproves only Craig’s restricted (insular) version of the corticocentric theory.
